 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. It's time for Game No. 4 of the Golden State Warriors season … and hopefully, Win No. 1. It won't be easy, though, as the Dubs are taking on superstar Nikola Jokić and the Denver Nuggets, on the road.
 There's good news, though: the Dubs are getting some reinforcements. After not playing Steph Curry, Draymond Green, Brandin Podziemski, or Al Horford in Saturday's loss to the Phoenix Suns , all four of those players are off the injury report in this one.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Here's the full injury report for both squads:
 Warriors
 Out — Kristaps Porziņģis (not with team) 
 No news is emphatically not good news in the case of Kristaps Porziņģis. It does feel like we've seen the last of him wearing a Warriors jersey, but that might be pessimistic of me. We're still waiting for an update … any update.
 Out — Jimmy Butler III (right ACL repair surgery) 
 Out — Moses Moody (left patellar tendon repair surgery) 
 Nothing new for either of these two. They'll be out for a few more months, at the minimum.
 Available — Gui Santos (left knee tendinitis) 
 Available — Charles Bassey (right patellar tendinopathy) 
 Available — Brandon Williams (left low back soreness) 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Santos, Bassey, and Williams all played on Saturday, and Bassey and Williams in particular player quite well. They're not 100%, but they're good to go for this game.
 Nuggets
 Out — Julian Strawther (left knee sprain) 
 Strawther, who was taken 29th overall in 2023, figures to play a huge role on Denver's team this year. Unfortunately, he suffered a knee injury in camp, and will likely be out until sometime around early December.
 Out — Spencer Jones (bilateral hamstring injury management) 
 Jones, who went undrafted out of Stanford, had a breakout second season a year ago. He's yet to make his season debut this year, but should be back on the court soon.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Out — Alpha Diallo (right wrist sprain/personal reasons) 
 Not often you see the injury/personal reasons combo. Hopefully everything is okay with Diallo, a 29-year old rookie.
 Doubtful — Cameron Johnson (right ankle sprain) 
 Johnson hasn't been as good with the Nuggets as he was before being traded by the Brooklyn Nets, but he's still a quality shooter, and one of Denver's starting five. It will be a hit for the Nuggets if he's unable to play.
 Enjoy the game, everyone. It tips off at 7:00 p.m. PT on NBC Sports Bay Area.
